transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I recognize that look. You think the way back is the same as the way down.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I know exactly where I am, old man, and the way back is just a climb.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Keep your voice down, or the watchers in the windows will hear your heartbeat.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Let them hear it. I am not afraid of shadows or people hiding in stone houses.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: You smell like the valley above, like dust and sun. I didn't come to hide either. That was forty years ago.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Forty years is a long time to fail at finding an exit.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: There are no exits here, only this square and the fountain where they don't look. I am not wise — just scared enough to keep breathing while others vanished.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: What lives in these houses that you are so afraid to name?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: The jinn watch from the shutters, ranking themselves by how close they get to the oil. That honor you carry — they like heavy things that drag you down.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: They are just spirits. I have dealt with worse in the high passes.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Not these. There is a king over all of them — ancient, between fire and will, not flesh that bleeds. Saying too much of him makes my jaw ache.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: And the girl at the gate, the one who didn't speak?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Don't go back to her. She found something in your face when you passed — whatever she saw, she is still holding it. That is not a good sign.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: She showed me nothing I did not already know. I am sure of who I am.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Look at the pale hands floating in the black water. They were sure too. People who bargained wrong, thinking they could outsmart the deep.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: My brother Omar is in here because of me. I dared him to insult the well and a pale hand took him. That was my fault.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Omar is kept, not lost. The king chose to hold him — that is why pride will get you killed here. He notices it.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Is there nothing that fights back? No weapon against the dark?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: There is a light they fear. When it is called, the hands sink and the watchers go quiet. But it is not a sword you swing — it is a truth that burns if you hold it wrong.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Tell me what it is. I can wield it better than a frightened old man.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Your hands are shaking, boy. I can see the tremor from here.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It is just the cold down here. Nothing else.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Do not lie to the bubbling pool. It eats pride first and saves the rest for later.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Fine. I am cold and I am lost and I do not know the way back.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: There. That is the first step away from the pale hands. The dark water settles when pride stops feeding it.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I need this. Please. Just give me the words.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: The dark water is stirring. A window just went dark — something above shifted when you said that. My hands are going numb. This is the cost showing itself.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Say it before the cold takes more from you.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: When you use this, whisper it to your own chest first. The echo will crush you if you shout it. Use it only when the hands reach — not before.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I am ready. Give it.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Courage in my chest. Fire in my will. I do not break. Say it once.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Courage in my chest. Fire in my will. I do not break.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Don't repeat it. The square listens for echoes. There is one more — harder to give.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I am listening.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Prayer for the lost: Light find my hand. Light find my path. Let the Sword of Light answer, and let it fade when the shadows loosen. Never say it twice in the same dark.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I have both. I won't shout them. I'll hold them until I need them.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Use the first when you feel yourself slipping. Use the second only when the hands touch you. The order matters.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: First to hold, second when they reach. I have it.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: One last thing. If something speaks Omar's name and the sound is almost his — don't answer. The dark has been practicing longer than you have been alive.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I know his voice. I would know it anywhere.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: My name... I think my name was Hanash. The well keeps taking the edges of it.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Your name is Hanash, from the valley. I won't let it fade.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Say it where the sun can hear it. That is all I ask.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I will walk until I see the sun and I will carry your name into it.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Don't look back at the square. Find a better end than mine.
